request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient History:

A 64-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital after experiencing right back pain for 6 days. She was evaluated in the emergency outpatient unit of our hospital 5 days PTA for concern of aortic dissection, infected arterial aneurysm, and purulent arthritis. Blood cultures taken at the time revealed methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE). She refused hospitalization and returned home until MRSE was once again detected in two sets of repeated blood cultures and she was admitted to our hospital.

Hospital Course:

On admission, the patient had a systolic murmur at the left sternal border and a punctate spot hemorrhage in the palpebral conjunctiva. Prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) was the suspected diagnosis based on PMH of aortic valve replacement, a physical examination of systolic cardiac murmur, and conjunctival hemorrhage. Trans-esophageal echocardiography (TEE) confirmed vegetations on her aortic valve, with a diagnosis of PVE. Vancomycin was started immediately on day 1. A repeated blood culture on day 5 was positive, but turned negative on day 8. Rifampicin was added on day 13 to decrease bacterial burden. Vancomycin was switched to teicoplanin on day 19 due to leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and fever, and rifampicin was discontinued due to a subsequent rash. Blood cultures taken on day 20 were negative, indicating successful treatment.

Discharge Instructions:

The patient underwent aortic valve re-replacement on day 33, and was discharged on day 50 with good postoperative recovery. The patient is advised to follow up with her physician in 4-6 weeks for further evaluation.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

Vancomycin followed by rifampicin and teicoplanin, with successful aortic valve re-replacement.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is prosthetic valve endocarditis, caused by MRSE, in a patient with an aortic valve replacement.

In ICD-10-AM, endocarditis of a prosthetic valve is classified to T82.6, "Infection and inflammatory reaction due to cardiac valve prosthesis". That sits in Chapter XIX (injury, poisoning and certain other consequences of external causes) under complications of cardiac and vascular prosthetic devices. The infecting organism would be added with B95-B96 as an additional code, and I33.0 (acute and subacute infective endocarditis) is not the code used for this.

The category is T82, with T82.6 as the specific code.

CODE: T82
